title: ai_tool_governor plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `ai_tool_governor` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component AiToolGovernorConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

AiToolGovernorCallerScopeList.description: Per-tool caller-identity scope (ai_tool_governor allowed_consumers / denied_consumers by Consumer username, allowed_groups / denied_groups by Consumer acl_groups). Evaluated after a per-tool deny or dry_run and before argument checks and approval. A denied_* match denies; with any allowed_* list configured the caller must match an allowed consumer or group; with any scope configured, a request without a mapped Consumer is denied. A tool definition outside the caller's scope is refused like a denied tool. Runtime admission enforces a stricter 512 UTF-8 byte entry cap (OpenAPI maxLength counts Unicode characters).

AiToolGovernorConfig.description: Plugin: ai_tool_governor — Deterministic allow/deny/approval policy for AI tool/function calls. Inspects request tool definitions across every provider shape (OpenAI tools[].function.name / functions[].name, Anthropic tools[].name, Google tools[].functionDeclarations[].name, Bedrock toolConfig.tools[].toolSpec.name), buffered response tool calls (OpenAI choices[].message.tool_calls[] and legacy function_call, OpenAI Responses output[] function_call items, Anthropic content[] tool_use blocks, Google candidates[].content.parts[].functionCall, Cohere v2 message.tool_calls[], Bedrock Converse output.message.content[].toolUse), streaming SSE tool-call deltas in the OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses (response.output_item.added / response.function_call_arguments.delta, with every .done / response.completed restatement required to match the accumulated call exactly), Anthropic (content_block_start / input_json_delta), Cohere v2 (tool-call-start / tool-call-delta), and Google shapes (held until complete and cleared by policy/approval, then released — or the stream is cut with an SSE error event, never leaking the held call), and optionally MCP tools/call and A2A JSON-RPC methods. A payload carrying a tool-call marker this plugin cannot read is ungovernable and fails closed in enforce mode by default (see unknown_shape_action). Complements ai_semantic_firewall (which catches intent): every decision here is a deterministic function of names, arguments, JSON Schema, regexes, identity, and an optional approval webhook. In enforce mode, governed bodies the plugin cannot inspect fail closed: Content-Encoding'd, oversized (>4 MiB), non-UTF-8, or unparseable JSON request bodies are rejected when request inspection is enabled, oversized JSON responses are rejected, a JSON response that is well-formed but beyond the inspection parser's nesting/numeric limits is rejected (malformed JSON is still forwarded), an SSE event that is not valid UTF-8 or carries such JSON cuts the stream, and streaming holds past the 4 MiB cap cut the stream. Configuration is strict: unknown root, inspect, tool-policy, blocked-pattern, approval, response, and observability properties are rejected (with path-qualified diagnostics). The free-form `tools` name map and arbitrary per-tool `json_schema` document remain open. Does not execute tools or replace mcp_gateway/A2A routing. HTTP-family only.

enabled.description: When false the plugin is inert (no buffering, no inspection), and policy field *values* are ignored — but unknown property names are still rejected at every fixed-shape layer.
When false the plugin is inert (no buffering, no inspection).

mode.description: enforce rejects/cuts blocked tool calls; dry_run evaluates and emits metadata but never rejects and never calls the approval webhook (safe rollout).

default_action.description: Action for a tool with no explicit policy entry. tools may be empty only when default_action governs (deny/require_approval).

unknown_shape_action.description: Posture for a governed payload that carries a live tool-call marker (tool_calls / toolCalls / tool_use / toolUse / function_call / functionCall member names, or a block tagged type: tool_use / function_call / tool-call) from which no call could be extracted — a provider tool-call shape this plugin cannot read — or, when calls WERE extracted, a marker outside every location the extractors read (a second call a normalizing client may honor; markers inside an extracted call's own arguments never count). deny (default) treats it as ungovernable: enforce rejects the body or cuts the stream, dry_run forwards. allow forwards it as if no tool call were present. BOTH settings record the fixed ai_tool_governor.uninspectable_reason=unrecognized_tool_call_shape observation without claiming a decision, so an unreadable shape is never silently permitted. Payloads with no tool-call marker at all (ordinary REST JSON on a shared proxy, embeddings/moderations responses, content-only completions) are out of scope under both settings.

inspect.description: Independently toggled inspection surfaces. At least one must be enabled. Unknown surface switches are rejected.

request_tool_definitions.description: Reject/dry-run requests that expose disallowed tool definitions to the model.

response_tool_calls.description: Govern tool calls in buffered (non-streaming) responses. At most 64 concrete tool calls are governed per request/response/SSE batch (unconditional; applies to allow/deny/redact_args/require_approval/dry_run).

streaming_response_tool_calls.description: Govern OpenAI SSE tool-call deltas. Held tool-call frames are released only after policy/approval clears the call; a block cuts the stream with a terminal SSE error event. Duplicate choice/tool indexes, empty-string or non-string IDs, conflicting IDs, or an ID introduced after an untagged fragment are ungovernable and fail closed in enforce mode. JSON null for tool_calls[].id is treated as omitted (same as a missing field). At most 64 concrete tool calls are governed per SSE batch. In streaming, a redact_args match fails closed (denies) since mid-stream surgical redaction of split-JSON arguments is out of scope.

mcp_tool_calls.description: Inspect MCP JSON-RPC tools/call request bodies directly (params.name + params.arguments), including calls inside JSON-RPC batch arrays. When params.arguments is omitted, the governor normalizes it to {} before required-arg / regex / hash / approval / JSON Schema evaluation (MCP zero-argument calls). Provider response shapes that omit function.arguments are not normalized. With mcp_gateway aggregate_router on the same proxy, policy identity stays the public namespaced tool name across the gateway's trusted upstream-name rewrite; final arguments are still rechecked and unrelated name changes fail closed.

a2a_methods.description: Govern A2A JSON-RPC method names against the tools policy map (params carried as arguments).

tools.description: Per-tool policy, keyed by a non-empty tool name (may be namespaced, e.g. github.create_pr, or an MCP/A2A method name) or by a glob containing `*` (e.g. github.*, *delete*). `*` matches any run of characters including none (it crosses `.`, `/`, and `_`), anchored at both ends. Precedence: an exact key always wins; among matching globs the one with the most literal (non-`*`) bytes wins, then fewer wildcards, then byte order of the key. At most 256 glob keys, each at most 256 UTF-8 bytes; globs are never A2A aliases. policy_ids metadata records the governing key. When composed with mcp_gateway aggregate_router, keys remain the public namespaced names: a trusted public-to-upstream rewrite is remapped for the final-body recheck only when the final wire name exactly matches that staged upstream alias; final arguments are still re-evaluated and unrelated name changes fail closed. The tool-name map is intentionally free-form; each policy object is closed.

action.description: allow forwards; deny blocks; redact_args replaces blocked_arg_patterns matches with redaction_placeholder (buffered path); require_approval calls the approval webhook; dry_run forwards and records ai_tool_governor.decision=dry_run distinctly from a real allow. At most 64 concrete tool calls are governed per request/response/SSE batch regardless of action.

risk.description: Risk band surfaced as ai_tool_governor.risk (max across a batch) and in approval requests.

max_arg_bytes.description: Deny when the raw arguments string exceeds this many bytes.

required_args.description: Deny when any listed key is absent from the parsed arguments object.

name.description: Pattern identifier; substituted into redaction_placeholder {name}. OpenAPI maxLength: 256 counts Unicode characters; runtime admission enforces a stricter 256 UTF-8 byte cap.

regex.description: Regex matched against the raw arguments string and, when the raw text contains a JSON escape, also against its JSON-decoded views (the canonical re-serialization and every decoded string, member names included), so an escaped spelling such as a unicode-escaped underscore cannot hide a match. Under a non-redact action a match in any view denies; under redact_args a raw match is redacted, and a match visible only in a decoded view (which raw-text redaction cannot remove) denies instead. Patterns that match empty input are rejected at config load; contextual zero-length matches fail closed at runtime.

blocked_arg_patterns.description: Named regexes screening tool arguments. At least one entry is required when action=redact_args. At most 32 patterns per tool; every append is checked before allocation and redacted output is capped at the 4 MiB inspectable body limit.

json_schema.description: JSON Schema (validated with the jsonschema crate) the parsed arguments must satisfy, else deny. Intentionally open — arbitrary JSON Schema keywords are allowed; do not set additionalProperties: false here.

approval.description: Approval webhook, required when any policy can reach require_approval.

endpoint_url.description: http/https URL POSTed with request_id, consumer, principal (the authority-qualified caller: {kind: consumer, namespace, id} for a mapped Consumer, or {kind: external, subject, mechanism, authority} where authority is the opaque hex digest of the verifying authority), proxy, model, provider, tool_name, arguments_hash, risk (and raw arguments only when include_arguments=true). An http:// URL is admitted only to a loopback IP literal host written as a dotted-quad 127.d.d.d or [::1] (URL userinfo does not count as part of the host) unless allow_plaintext is true, because a cleartext channel lets a man-in-the-middle forge allow verdicts. The URI scheme is case-insensitive (runtime parsing normalizes it before the http/https check), so HTTPS://host/path is admitted exactly like https://host/path. Response: {"decision":"allow|deny"} or {"allow":true|false}, optional approval_id. Response bodies are capped at 64 KiB.

timeout_ms.description: Per-request approval webhook timeout (max 30000). A batch resolves its approvals with at most 8 webhook calls in flight and the whole batch is capped at 30s of approval wait; after an enforce-mode block, no further webhook call in that batch is started (calls already in flight complete). Calls identical in name and arguments within one batch share one resolution when cache_ttl_seconds > 0. At most 64 concrete tool calls are governed per request/response/SSE batch. Dropping the governing future (client cancel) cancels any in-flight approval HTTP call.

cache_ttl_seconds.description: TTL for caching an approval decision keyed by consumer+principal+proxy+model+provider+tool+arguments, so equal subject strings verified by different authorities never share a decision. 0 disables caching. The cache is bounded (4096 entries); at capacity expired entries are purged and new decisions are not cached rather than growing memory.

fail_on_error.description: Behavior when the approval endpoint cannot be evaluated: reject fails closed, warn/allow fail open.

include_arguments.description: Include the raw tool arguments in the approval request body. Off by default so secrets are not sent.

headers.description: Extra request headers for the approval call (for example an Authorization credential). A value is a literal, or a whole-value ${FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>} reference resolved from the process environment at the first approval call (an unset or invalid secret is an approval endpoint error handled by fail_on_error; config validation does not need the live secret). Names must be valid HTTP header names, unique case-insensitively, and may not be content-type, content-length, host, transfer-encoding, connection, keep-alive, proxy-connection, te, trailer, upgrade, or X-Ferrum-Hops; values must be valid header values. Runtime admission additionally enforces the reference namespace and a stricter 8192 UTF-8 byte value cap (OpenAPI maxLength counts Unicode characters). Values are never logged or echoed in diagnostics.

allow_plaintext.description: Admit an http:// endpoint_url whose host is not a loopback IP literal. Verdicts, any headers credential, and (with include_arguments) raw arguments then cross the network in clear.

deny_status_code.description: HTTP error status (400-599) returned for a deterministic tool policy denial in enforce mode. Uninspectable governed bodies fail closed with 502.

redaction_placeholder.description: Template for redacted argument matches; {name} is replaced with the matched pattern name. OpenAPI maxLength: 256 counts Unicode characters; runtime admission enforces a stricter 256 UTF-8 byte cap. Redacted argument output is capped at the 4 MiB inspectable body limit.

streaming_deny_event.description: Emit a terminal SSE error event when cutting a streamed tool call.

emit_metadata.description: Emit ai_tool_governor.* transaction metadata (enabled, mode, decision, tool_names, risk, policy_ids, approval_id, arguments_hashes, redacted_tools).

hash_arguments.description: Emit SHA-256 hashes of tool arguments as ai_tool_governor.arguments_hashes. Raw arguments are never placed in metadata.

max_argument_log_bytes.description: When > 0, log up to this many bytes of a blocked call's raw arguments at debug for audit. 0 keeps raw arguments out of logs entirely.
